input: # KEY CONFLICTS. TOML does not allow a key to be redefined, and every
# runtime refuses one with toml_key_conflict. The values a runtime WOULD
# have built are the reason the code exists: before the check, a value
# redefined as a table was overwritten by an empty table, and an array of
# tables redefined as a table lost either the array or the table,
# depending on the port -- silent data loss on an invalid document, and
# nothing reported it. Go accepted every row below until 2026-10; its
# engine now passes a coded error raised inside a grammar action through
# with the code intact, so the check reaches the reader there too.
# A value used again as a table: through a header, a dotted header, and a
# dotted key in an inline table.
# A value used again as a table-array header.
# A table redefined as an array of tables, and an array of tables redefined
# CONTROLS. Descending into an existing table, into the implicit table a
# dotted key or a deeper header created, or into the last element of an
# existing array of tables is legitimate; four valid corpus documents do
# exactly this, and a first cut of the check rejected all four.
